title: Camp 4 close: he goes before you (Mark 16)
hook: the women at the tomb hear he goes before you into Galilee

segments.voice: Yesterday, centurion: a Roman soldier at the cross said indeed this man was the son of God. Today camp four ends, at an empty tomb.

Very early on the first day of the week, with the sun now risen, three women walk to the tomb with spices to anoint the body: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. They had watched the crucifixion from a distance. On the way they worry about something practical: who will roll the stone away for us? It was very big. They're not expecting a miracle; they're expecting a heavy rock and a dead friend. Then they look up, and the stone is already rolled back.
screen: `SUNRISE, THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.` → `WHO WILL ROLL THE STONE AWAY?` → `IT'S ALREADY ROLLED BACK.`

segments.voice: First, the news. Inside, a young man in a white robe is sitting on the right, and they're terrified. He says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be not affrighted; you seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified: he is risen, he is not here." Second, the errand: "But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, as he told you." And Peter: the one who wept by the fire, named on purpose. Galilee is where it all began: the lake, the boats, the ordinary towns. He's not waiting in the Temple. He's gone ahead, back to the everyday. Third, the ending. The women run from the tomb, trembling, "and they said nothing to any man; for they were afraid." In some of the oldest manuscripts that survive, Mark stops right there. Later manuscripts carry a longer ending, with the risen Jesus appearing first to Mary Magdalene and sending the eleven out to the whole world. The Catholic Church receives that longer ending as inspired Scripture, and scholars still debate who wrote it and when. Either way, the story didn't stay untold. You're hearing it. Fourth, look back. This camp was the text itself. The Psalms: two ways, the Lord ruleth me, be still, have mercy, out of the depths, let every spirit praise. Then Mark straight through: the beginning, fishers of men, the sower, peace be still, Ephphatha, who do you say I am, Bartimaeus, the widow's mites, Abba, truly this man. Tomorrow a new camp begins, the depths, starting with how Catholics pray when words run out.
screen: `HE IS RISEN, HE IS NOT HERE.` · `TELL HIS DISCIPLES, AND PETER.` · `THEY SAID NOTHING; THEY WERE AFRAID.` · `THE PSALMS, THEN MARK STRAIGHT THROUGH.` · then, large: `HE GOETH BEFORE YOU INTO GALILEE.`

segments.voice: Your Galilee is the place you spend most of your days: a kitchen, a desk, a car, a checkout line. Picture it, and imagine someone has gone ahead and is already there, waiting; Catholics say the risen Christ goes before them into ordinary life. If you pray, you can ask to see him there; if you don't, just picture walking into your ordinary place expecting something good.
Risen. What the young man in white tells the women at the tomb: he is risen, he is not here. Today's word.
Your line: he goes before you. The tomb is empty. Camp four, complete.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the resurrection at the Easter Vigil and on every Sunday, and the resurrection is the first Glorious Mystery of the rosary; Mark 16 is read at the Easter Vigil in the year of Mark.

chat.says: What did the women find at Jesus's tomb that Sunday morning?
options: The stone rolled back, and a young man in white: he is risen.
The stone still sealed, so they waited for help to move it.
An empty tomb, and a note telling them to go to the Temple.
chat.meaning: The stone was rolled back, and a young man in white said: he is risen, he is not here; he goes before you into Galilee.

Mary Magdalene.meaning: a follower who watched the cross and came to the tomb

Salome.meaning: one of the three women at the tomb

Galilee.meaning: where it all began: the lake and ordinary towns
